While the viewership of "Comics Unleashed" is a fraction of the audience that Stephen Colbert had, it was reported that CBS now expects to make a $15 million profit in the same time slot due to the massive cost-cutting.

item.title: WNBA veteran Natasha Cloud smears Fever fan with wild domestic abuse claim over pointing finger at A'ja Wilson
item.description: Natasha Cloud publicly implied a Fever fan is a domestic abuser after a baseline dustup, despite arena security clearing the spectator of wrongdoing.
item.content:encoded:
The WNBA’s favorite narrative — that players are perpetual victims — just reached peak delusion thanks to Chicago Sky guard Natasha Cloud.

Following Tuesday’s baseline dust-up after a foul on Fever guard Sophie Cunningham, Las Vegas Aces star A’ja Wilson confronted a fan, leading Cloud to take to Threads and smear both the Indiana Fever organization and the spectator.

Cloud demanded the Fever publicly condemn the fan, despite arena security clearing him of any wrongdoing. League guidelines explicitly prohibit players from stepping off the court or entering spectator space to confront fans.

WNBA REFS MISS OPPORTUNITY TO EJECT A'JA WILSON OVER MELTDOWN, ENTERING STANDS

Yet, as reported by OutKick’s Dan Zaksheske, the WNBA excused Wilson under the absurd claim that she was standing in a "player escape lane."

"[And] imma be the one to say it's time for Indy as an organization to start denouncing some s——t," Cloud posted, defending Wilson and dragging the Fever.

Then came the wild leap.

Cloud launched slanderous accusations about the spectator’s personal life based on nothing more than a brief clip of him pointing a finger.

"Mind you he is the 2nd man to take a step towards the court... Wife had to yank him down out of embarrassment," Cloud wrote.

And then she crossed into reckless slander:

"Even worse.... if he's willing to do that s——t in public to a woman he doesn't know....how do you think he acts in his home?"

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The Sky guard closed her rant by framing players as victims: "No it's not our job to continue to fix the problems. Our job is to hoop & to be safe doing it."

A veteran WNBA player publicly implied a fan is a domestic abuser because he pointed a finger after a whistle: pure character assassination. Without a shred of evidence, Cloud casually weaponized domestic violence allegations against a fan who was simply cheering for his home team.

This isn't Cloud's first time acting as a courtside moral crusader, either. Just last month, she instigated a baseline scene with former NBA center Enes Kanter Freedom in Chicago, marching over to confront him at his seat.

In today's WNBA environment, facts are secondary to maintaining the preferred narrative.

ENES KANTER FREEDOM SENDS LETTER TO WNBA REQUESTING REVIEW OF SKY EJECTION INCIDENT, FULL TICKET REFUND

A vocal contingent of players and media members operates under a bad-faith assumption, labeling Indiana’s fanbase as toxic. You have to ask the obvious question: is this constant outrage really about fan decorum, or is it because Indiana rostered the two most popular white players in the league, Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham?

Except the actual facts tell a completely different story.

Gainbridge Fieldhouse arena security conducted an immediate, onsite investigation into the baseline incident.

Security guards interviewed witnesses, reviewed footage, and officially confirmed that the spectator committed zero violations of the Fan Code of Conduct. He was cleared on the spot and remained in his seat for the rest of Indiana’s playoff win.

Yet for Cloud, official clearance means nothing. The assumption of guilt is permanent because it fits the narrative: Fever fans are bad, players are infallible and standing up to point is dangerous.

When a WNBA veteran does it to a fan who was officially cleared of any wrongdoing, the league office stays silent. Protecting the narrative will always come ahead of the truth.

item.title: Judge permanently dismisses Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool vandalism case against former Olympian
item.description: Judge Todd Edelman's ruling prevents the Justice Department from refiling charges against Hearn, who was accused of damaging the pool’s peeling coating.
item.content:encoded:
A judge on Thursday permanently dismissed the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool vandalism case against former Olympian David Hearn, who was accused of damaging the costly $14 million renovation project in June.

D.C. Superior Court Judge Todd Edelman’s ruling marks the end of a monthslong legal battle that included President Donald Trump criticizing U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro after she moved to voluntarily dismiss the federal charges in late July.

Unlike Pirro’s decision, Thursday’s ruling was made with prejudice, meaning the Department of Justice (DOJ) cannot refile the same charges against Hearn.

Edelman rejected prosecutors’ request to preserve the possibility of recharging Hearn if new evidence surfaced, finding that existing investigative findings were sufficient to show the damage stemmed from a flawed renovation job.

TRUMP SAYS HE 'DISAGREES 100%' WITH U.S. ATTORNEY JEANINE PIRRO OVER REFLECTING POOL CASE

"In the exceptional circumstances posed by this case, the government has no right to retain the ability to compound the errors it has already made, or even to threaten to do so, at Mr. Hearn’s expense," Edelman said. "This case must be dismissed with prejudice, and the government must thus be barred from reinstituting this charge against Mr. Hearn."

Hearn’s counsel described the decision as a victory for "an innocent American seeking justice."

"This case never should have been brought in the first place. This was a miscarriage of justice, and what happened to Mr. Hearn is an outrage that should shock every American," Hearn’s counsel said in a statement.

"This administration chose to pursue an unjust prosecution against Mr. Hearn. It should not get repeated chances to wield the power of criminal prosecution against someone who should never have been prosecuted."

Fox News Digital reached out to the White House for comment. 

WHITE HOUSE ASKS DOJ TO CONSIDER NEW PROSECUTION IN REFLECTING POOL CASE

Hearn was arrested June 19 and later indicted on one felony count of destruction of property for allegedly damaging the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool’s lining.

Prosecutors alleged that Hearn was seen grabbing and tugging on a loose section of the pool’s coating, reportedly causing about $1,000 in damage. Officials added that he continued to do so even after National Park Service employees urged him to stop.

TRUMP DOUBLES DOWN ON REFLECTING POOL VANDALISM ALLEGATIONS, CITES NEW WITNESS ACCOUNT

Trump has strictly maintained that the pool was vandalized, criticizing Pirro’s decision to drop the case as "hastily made."

"Anybody who thinks the Reflecting Pool wasn’t vandalized should go back to Law School!" Trump previously said in a post on Truth Social.

"People were on their knees with their hands in the water at the exact location of the ‘slashes.’ Additionally, there were witnesses to the VANDALISM, and the flexible areas of the material were cut with a knife."

The DOJ moved to dismiss the indictment after evidence from the Department of the Interior revealed that the damage was caused by a "rushed and botched" installation by contractor Atlantic Industrial Coatings ahead of the America 250 celebrations, court filings said.

According to the documents, Hearn touched peeling perimeter "overspray" material that was already peeling and had minimal economic value.

Hearn subsequently requested that the case be dismissed with prejudice, permanently barring the government from refiling the charges.

item.title: Amish face New York vaccine mandate in Supreme Court fight, might have to ‘pack their wagons’
item.description: First Liberty Institute is urging the Supreme Court to intervene as Amish families face crushing fines under New York's school vaccine mandate.
item.content:encoded:
New York’s elimination of religious exemptions for school vaccine mandates is threatening to drive Amish families from the state, according to First Liberty Institute attorney Hiram Sasser, who is urging the Supreme Court to intervene in the ongoing legal battle.

For decades, New York allowed religious exemptions for schoolchildren. But the state repealed that exemption in 2019, leaving Amish families and their small private schools facing vaccination requirements and potentially crippling fines. 

The 2nd Circuit upheld the law in June, and the Amish have since asked the Supreme Court to take up the case.

"For decades, New York had a religious exemption for their vaccine mandate that they had on the books, and it protected the Amish who've been there for over 200 years," Sasser told Fox News Digital Wednesday.

‘COVID 2.0’: LAWMAKERS PUSH BACK ON SWEEPING HEALTH 'POLICE POWER' IN KEY BATTLEGROUND STATE

"And it's just such a shame that New York is one of the only states in America that decided that they wanted to get rid of their vaccine religious exemption and to try to impose it on everybody, including private schools and, unfortunately, hitting the Amish who have their own ‘Little House on the Prairie’-style schools that they have on their farms," Sasser said. 

"And, for whatever reason, New York decided that they were going to start enforcing this requirement on the Amish who, frankly, just don't participate in these kinds of things. And instead of just leaving the Amish alone, New York decided to enforce it."

Sasser said the state has put "crushing fines" on the Amish, which are endangering their farms and even the ability to stay in New York.

CATHOLIC NUNS CARING FOR DYING PATIENTS FIGHT NEW YORK TRANS RULE, FACE JAIL TIME

"We're representing the Amish, and I got to tell you, when they filed their declaration with the court, it was, it's handwritten because that's how they do it, and they work as a community together. … They want to be really good citizens. They want to do their part for the state of New York, for America," Sasser said. 

"They want to live quiet, humble lives, be good neighbors, but New York is putting them to a religious test that we should never put the Amish to."

Sasser said the dispute is about more than vaccines and could determine whether the Amish can continue living out their faith and traditional way of life in New York.

DOJ BACKS NUNS CARING FOR DYING CANCER PATIENTS IN FIGHT AGAINST NEW YORK TRANS IDEOLOGY MANDATE

"These are the Amish schools like ‘Little House on the Prairie,’ if you've ever seen that show. It's like that, and they're carrying out a way of life that was, that predominated across America for a long time, but we've all sort of moved on with modern things. But they're holding the fort, so to speak, of a way of life that we all used to live," Sasser said.

"I have no idea why the state of New York wants to go in there and shut them down," Sasser continued. "Frankly, the Amish would just like to be left alone, but they still really want to be positive members of the community. They want to serve their neighbors, they want to be good citizens, and New York just won't seem to let them do that unless they violate their religious beliefs."

First Liberty said it is awaiting a response from the other side, then a decision from the Supreme Court.

In a statement to Fox News Digital, the New York Department of Health said, "The state’s responsibility is to protect public health, keep New Yorkers and their families safe and enforce the law fairly and equitably. While we cannot comment on pending litigation, the department is committed to eliminating serious illness and unnecessary deaths caused by vaccine-preventable diseases. 

"The department continues to provide community outreach and education on the safety of immunizations. New York’s school immunization requirements are based in science and protect the health and well-being of all New Yorkers."

Fox News Digital reached out to New York Gov. Kathy Hochul and Commissioner of Education Betty Rosa.

item.title: Is the Taco Bell ultra marathon the toughest event in sports and why is the answer a resounding yes?
item.description: The International Taco Bell 50k requires runners to eat a Chalupa Supreme and Burrito Supreme across nine stops on a grueling 30-mile Denver run.
item.content:encoded:
There may be longer races, and there may be more prestigious races, but none require the intestinal fortitude — in the most literal sense — needed to complete the International Taco Bell 50k.

The 9th annual edition of the ultra marathon in Denver gets underway this weekend, and it will see runners traversing just over 30 miles, while making pit stops at a minimum of nine of the ten Taco Bell locations along the route where they must order a menu item and finish it.

And better yet, it's not sanctioned by the company. They're just out there for the love of the game.

MONSTROUS WENDY'S BURGER RETURNS, DARING CUSTOMERS TO DEVOUR 9 PATTIES IN 9 MINUTES

Of course, my first thought was that there has to be a way to go easy on the food, but the rules require competitors to eat some serious heavy hitters.

Drinks do not count as food, and all competitors have to eat a Chalupa Supreme or Crunchwrap Supreme by the fourth stop. By the eighth stop, they have to have polished off a Burrito Supreme or Nachos Bell Grande, but other than that, it's fair game.

PROFESSIONAL EATER INHALES A BURRITO TO RECLAIM A TITLE SHE HAD LOST AS WORLD'S FASTEST

Just finish in 11 hours without puking or using any on-course Pepto, Alka-Seltzer, Pepcid A/C, Mylanta, and congratulations, you've completed a race with a higher DNF rate than the 100-mile Leadville 100 Trail Race.

I can't wrap my head around this race. The last thing I ever want to do after eating Taco Bell is exercise, and I'm eating a fraction of what these athletes will gobble up.

'A WIN IS A WIN' SAYS ATHLETE WHO DIDN'T LET A LITTLE DIARRHEA KEEP HER FROM FINISHING IN FIRST PLACE

Hell, if someone said, "Now that you've polished off that Baja Blast and seven-layer burrito, how about doing a quick lap around the restaurant," I'd have to respectfully explain that that is a very bad idea.

And here's a detail no one even seems to pick up on that makes this even more diabolical: it's in Denver.

So, imagine running 30 miles with a stomach full of every conceivable combination and permutation of tortilla, meat, and cheese, and then doing it at altitude.

This should be an Olympic sport.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

I mean, if breaking was, why not?

But if that still doesn't seem tough enough for you, there are ways to make it harder. The Baja Blast Challenge requires runners to drink a total of 2 liters of the tropical-flavored soda.

Then, if you've got a stomach like a lead-lined bomb shelter, you can try the Diablo challenge, which involves eating each item with Diablo sauce and then doing a Diablo shooter at the finish line.

item.title: LA mayoral hopeful stumbles through favorite rappers from the city, host calls her 'media trained'
item.description: Nithya Raman hesitated naming favorite LA rappers on the "Higher Learning" podcast, drawing laughs and teasing ahead of the Los Angeles mayoral election.
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles mayoral candidate Nithya Raman hesitated while naming her favorite Los Angeles rappers during a Tuesday podcast interview, drawing laughter and teasing from the hosts weeks before voters decide whether she or incumbent Mayor Karen Bass will lead the nation's second-largest city.

Appearing on the "Higher Learning" podcast, Raman was asked to list her three favorite L.A. rappers. She first named the late Nipsey Hussle and co-host Van Lathan immediately ribbed the city councilmember over her answer.

"Wow. Look at you, media trained," Lathan said.

Raman, 45, then said she still listened to "‘90s rap," but paused as she tried to continue her list. As the hosts laughed, Lathan told her, "And okay, as you search for the names, keep going."

"I’m just shy," Raman said.

SEE IT: LA DEM CANDIDATES TORCHED BY DISGUSTED RESIDENTS AFTER ‘DISGRACEFUL’ DEBATE: ‘BOTH BAD’

Raman eventually added Snoop Dogg and Tupac Shakur. Lathan summed up her list as "Nip, Pac, Snoop," while Raman explained that the music was what she listened to alone in her car and described it as "the songs of my youth."

Lisa Cusack, President of the Don't L.A. My Burbank PAC, told Fox News Digital she believed the exchange undercut Raman’s efforts to portray herself as closely connected to Los Angeles culture.

"Interesting that Raman called illegal street vendors an ‘indispensable part’ of L.A.'s culture, but can’t name some of the city’s most famous rappers. Feels like someone’s giving her a script, because she’s not from L.A. and doesn’t actually know what the city’s about," Cusack said.

KAREN BASS APPEARS TO LIKEN SPENCER PRATT TO TRUMP AMID TIGHTENING LA MAYORAL RACE

Raman was born in India and came to the United States at age six. She later settled in Los Angeles and lives in Silver Lake, according to The Los Angeles Times. She was elected to the Los Angeles City Council in 2020 and currently represents the city's 4th district, including neighborhoods such as Hollywood, Sherman Oaks and Van Nuys.

Los Angeles County Republican Party Chairwoman Roxanne Hoge used the exchange to criticize Raman over the city’s business climate.

"I'd rather Raman be able to name her top three thriving L.A. businesses," Hoge said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "She can't."

SPENCER PRATT'S UNEXPECTED POLITICAL RISE FROM MTV VILLAIN TO KAREN BASS CHALLENGER

The podcast appearance came as Raman and Bass compete in the Nov. 3 runoff after Raman advanced from the June primary. Raman narrowly secured the second runoff spot behind Bass after passing Republican candidate and TV personality Spencer Pratt during the extended vote count, after Pratt led Raman on election night.

Raman has increasingly centered her campaign on dissatisfaction with City Hall's handling of homelessness, basic city services and the entertainment industry.

"I came into this race because I feel passionately about the future of Los Angeles and I feel frustration about the current state of the city. And I think that a third of voters is out there feeling those same things," Raman said.

Recently, Raman was pressed during a mayoral debate over her campaign’s decision to hire a consulting firm that previously worked with former Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner. A recent UC Berkeley Institute of Governmental Studies poll found Raman leading Bass 39% to 28% among likely Los Angeles voters, while 33% remained undecided. The online survey of 2,150 likely voters was conducted Sept. 15-20 and had a margin of error of approximately 3 percentage points.

Fox News Digital reached out to Bass for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Video shows Maine Wire reporter nearly being run over by car after confrontation
item.description: Video showed Maine Wire reporter Joe Sokol nearly being struck by a car outside an addiction treatment center Thursday morning as he was reporting.
item.content:encoded:

Sokol could then be heard reciting the suspect's license plate numbers through the knocked-down camera as the car kept driving.

The Maine Wire also showed additional footage which featured security footage of how close the vehicle approached Sokol, as well as Sokol approaching the center's owner, suggesting the suspect was connected.

HOW THE MEDIA, IN THE DIGITAL AGE, HELP FUEL A CLIMATE OF ANGER AND VIOLENCE

"I currently have an active death-threat investigation that has sat on the district attorney’s desk for more than a month," Sokol said. "I have been assaulted multiple times; one of those incidents resulted in a charge, which the state dropped last week. Violence and aggression toward Maine Wire reporters is never addressed in Bangor. About three weeks ago, my cameraman, Adam Stade, was nearly attacked by several homeless people in the city. One councilor’s wife — Michael Beck’s — actually asked the police to intervene regarding our coverage (attached). Most of the city council refuses to comment on the subject generally."

The conservative-leaning Maine Wire also released a statement honoring Sokol reacting well under pressure and providing additional detail regarding Sokol's investigation.

VULNERABLE DEM'S OWN AUDIT ADMITS MEDICAID OVERSIGHT FAILURE AMID MASSIVE STATEWIDE FRAUD SCANDAL

"Joe was there to ask questions about a methadone clinic that, according to The Maine Wire’s reporting, has received roughly $25 million in taxpayer funding via Medicaid. This is essentially a taxpayer-funded drug dealing operation at the heart of Bangor, Maine. We will continue to investigate this organization, its enablers, and the employees who appeared to be accessories after the fact rather than Good Samaritans," the statement read.

Thank you for your attention to this matter."

Fox News Digital has reached out to the Bangor Comprehensive Treatment Center for comment.
